div.p: Accounting Framework (Art. 831-1)
The annual accounts for the financial year ended {{ end of period }} are prepared in accordance with ANC Regulation No. 2014-03 on the general chart of accounts, version of 1 January 2026.
The basic method used for measuring items recognized in the accounts is the historical cost method.
General accounting conventions have been applied, in accordance with the prudence principle, based on the following assumptions:

ul.li: Going concern
Consistency of accounting methods from one year to the next
Accruals basis (matching principle)

div.p: Intangible and Tangible Fixed Assets (Art. 831-1)

Intangible assets are measured at their acquisition or production cost, taking into account the costs necessary to bring these assets into a condition for use, and after deducting trade discounts, rebates and settlement discounts obtained, with a view to their intended use.
Tangible fixed assets are measured at their acquisition cost, comprising:

ul.li: their purchase price (including non-recoverable customs duties and taxes, after deducting rebates, trade discounts and settlement discounts),
costs directly attributable to and incurred in bringing these assets into working condition for their intended use,
where applicable, the initial estimate of dismantling, removal and site restoration costs. Tangible fixed assets are measured at their production cost.

div.p: Interest on borrowings specific to the production of fixed assets is not included in the production cost of these assets.
The following decisions have been made regarding the presentation of the annual accounts:

ul.li: decomposable assets: the company has not been able to identify decomposable assets, or their decomposition does not have a material impact,
non-decomposable assets: taking advantage of the tolerance measures, the company has opted to retain the useful-life periods for depreciating non-decomposed assets.

div.p: Depreciation is calculated using the straight-line or declining-balance method, based on the expected useful life.
Financial Assets and Marketable Securities (Art. 831-1)
The gross value is the purchase cost, excluding incidental expenses. Where the inventory value is lower than the gross value, an impairment provision is recognized for the amount of the difference.

ul.li: Use of the equity method of valuation
Use of the exemption for valuing securities in the event of an abnormal and temporary decline.

div.p: Research and Development Costs (Art. 831-1)
Recognition as an expense:
Research and development expenses are recognized as an expense in the financial year in which they are incurred.
Inventory (Art. 831-1)
Inventory is measured using:

ul.li: (Choose one)
The first-in, first-out method (FIFO)
The weighted average cost method (WAC)
The standard cost method

div.p: The gross value of goods and supplies includes the purchase price and incidental expenses.
Manufactured products are valued at production cost, including consumption and direct and indirect production expenses, as well as depreciation of assets used in production.
The cost of idle capacity is excluded from the value of inventory.
Receivables and Payables (Art. 831-1)
Receivables and payables have been measured at their nominal value.

Receivables are, where applicable, impaired by way of a provision to reflect the collection difficulties they may give rise to. Provisions for potential impairment are determined by comparing the acquisition value with the probable realizable value.
Receivables and payables denominated in foreign currency are converted into euros based on the exchange rate at the invoice date.
Cash and Cash Equivalents (Art. 831-1)
Cash available on hand or in the bank is recorded at its nominal value.
Cash available in foreign currency is converted into euros based on the last exchange rate preceding the closing of the financial year.
Translation differences are recognized directly in the result for the year as a foreign exchange loss or gain.
Repayable Advances (Art. 831-1)

Advances received from public or private bodies to finance the Company's activities, the repayment of which is conditional, are presented on the liabilities side under "Other equity". The corresponding interest is presented on the liabilities side of the balance sheet under "Miscellaneous loans and financial debts".
Government Grants (Art. 831-1)
Government Grants: Prorated Recognition

The company has received grants that were recognized in operating income in proportion to the expenses incurred. As a result, grants receivable may be recorded in the accounts if the award agreement has been signed and expenses have been incurred but the grants have not yet been received. The portion of grants financing capitalized expenditure is recognized in operating income at the same pace as the depreciation of the related expenditure. The portion earned but not yet recognized in income is recorded in equity, under investment grants.
Government Grants: Non-prorated Recognition
Operating grants are recognized as income as soon as they are awarded.
Borrowings (Art. 831-1)
Loan issuance costs are, where applicable, recognized as an expense in the financial year in which the loans were granted.
Capital Increase Costs (Art. 831-1)
Capital issuance costs are recognized on the balance sheet, deducted from the share premium.
Retirement Indemnities (Art. 831-1)

The amounts of future payments corresponding to benefits granted to employees are measured using an actuarial method (ANC recommendation 2013-02), based on assumptions regarding salary trends, retirement age and mortality, and these estimates are then discounted to their present value.

These obligations are provided for on the liabilities side of the balance sheet. The calculation method used is method 1, in accordance with the provisions of the former CNC recommendation No. 2003-R.01.

The nature of the income and expenses recognized in the extraordinary result during the year is specified, distinguishing between:

ul.li: income and expenses directly linked to a major and unusual event
accounting entries of a purely tax-driven nature, as defined and provided for by the regulations of the Accounting Standards Authority
changes in accounting method that the entity is required to recognize in income, rather than in equity, due to the application of tax rules
corrections of errors, except where correcting an entry that was directly charged to equity.

div.p: The major and unusual event giving rise to the recognition of income and expenses directly linked to that event in the extraordinary result is described, indicating, where applicable, the amounts already recognized as a result of that event during prior years.
Tax Credits and Extraordinary Tax-Driven Adjustments (Art. 833-1 to 833-3)

div.h3: Tax Credits and Extraordinary Tax-Driven Adjustments
div.p: Where applicable, specify any tax change and its impact on the result for the year
Where applicable, detail and justify any extraordinary value adjustment on fixed assets or on current assets.
The impact on the result for the year of any tax change enacted between the balance sheet date and the date the accounts are prepared is disclosed.
The notes include information on the nature and amount of tax credits.
The notes include the following information:

ol.li: the detail and justification of extraordinary value adjustments on fixed assets linked to tax legislation
the detail and justification of extraordinary value adjustments on current assets linked to tax legislation.

div.p: Carryback of Losses and Tax Consolidation (Art. 833-4)

div.h3: Carryback of Losses and Tax Consolidation
div.p: Where applicable, specify any loss carryback made: nature, amount and accounting treatment of the corresponding receivable.

Where applicable, if {{ company name }} belongs to a tax-consolidated group, specify the corporate income tax allocation arrangements, the difference between the tax recognized and the tax due on a standalone basis, as well as the carryforward losses.
The notes include the following information:

ol.li: an indication of the nature, amount and accounting treatment of receivables resulting from the carryback of losses

the allocation of the total amount of income tax between ordinary result and extraordinary result, specifying in particular the tax bases and rates as well as tax credits, tax rebates and other offsets
the amount of items likely to give rise to a reduction or increase in the future income tax liability
an indication, even approximate, of the extent to which the result has been affected by tax-driven measurement departures adopted in order to obtain tax relief

for tax-consolidated entities, the minimum disclosures are as follows:
the arrangements for allocating corporate income tax based on the group's overall result
the difference between the tax recognized and the tax for the payment of which the entity is jointly and severally liable
the difference between the tax recognized and the tax that would have been borne in the absence of tax consolidation
the carryforward losses
the specific nature and content of the "Income tax" line item.

record.field: Transactions Not Concluded on Normal Market Terms

field.name: template_body
field.h2: Transactions Not Concluded on Normal Market Terms

div.p: Related Parties (Art. 834-1)
Where applicable, describe material transactions concluded on terms other than normal market terms.

p.strong: Information on transactions carried out with related parties
Nature of the relationship with the related party
Amount of transactions carried out with the related party during the year

div.p: The company provides a list of material transactions, within the meaning of Article R. 123-199-1 of the French Commercial Code, carried out by the company with related parties where these transactions were not concluded on normal market terms. This list includes the following information: the designation of the related party, the nature of the relationship with the related party, the amount of transactions carried out with the related party, and any other information on the transactions necessary to assess the company's financial position. Information on the various transactions may be aggregated by nature, except where separate information is necessary to understand the effects of transactions with related parties on the company's financial position.
However, this information is not required for transactions carried out:

ol.li: by the company with subsidiaries it wholly owns
between sister companies wholly owned by the same parent company.

div.p: Main Shareholders and Administrative Bodies - Small Entities and Simplified Real Regime (Art. 834-2)

p.strong: Information on transactions carried out with the main shareholders and the administrative, management or supervisory bodies
Nature of the relationship with the third party
Amount of transactions carried out with the third party during the year

div.p: Joint-stock companies falling under the small entity category provided for in Article L. 123-16 and the category provided for in Article L. 123-25 of the French Commercial Code disclose in the notes the list of transactions carried out between, on the one hand, the company and its main shareholders and, on the other hand, the company and the members of its administrative, management or supervisory bodies, where these transactions are material and were not concluded on normal market terms. This list includes the following information: the designation of the third party concerned, the nature of the relationship with the third party concerned, the amount of transactions carried out with the third party concerned, and any other information on the transactions necessary to assess the company's financial position. Information on the various transactions may be aggregated by nature, except where separate information is necessary to understand the effects of transactions with related parties on the company's financial position.

field.name: template_body
field.h2: Transactions and Commitments to Members of the Administrative, Management or Supervisory Bodies

div.p: Advances, Credits and Retirement Commitments (Art. 835-1)

Where applicable, specify the advances and credits granted to members of the administrative, management or supervisory bodies: terms granted, repayments made during the year, and amount of commitments made on their behalf.
Where applicable, specify the total amount, by category, of retirement commitments and similar benefits granted to members of the administrative, management or supervisory bodies.
For the members of the administrative, management or supervisory bodies, the total amount is disclosed, for each category, of:

ol.li: advances and credits granted to them, indicating the terms granted and the repayments made during the year, as well as the amount of commitments made on their behalf
retirement commitments and similar benefits contracted in their favor.

div.p: Remuneration (Art. 835-2)

The total amount of remuneration granted by {{ company name }} to the members of its administrative, management or supervisory bodies in respect of their duties for the financial year ended {{ end of period }} is shown below.

td.p: Valuation of options granted during the year

div.p: For the members of the administrative, management or supervisory bodies, the total amount, for each category, of remuneration granted in respect of their duties is disclosed. This information may not be provided where it would allow the situation of a specific member of these bodies to be identified.
Non-disclosure
Management has chosen not to disclose remuneration information, as doing so would effectively reveal the individual compensation of executives.

field.name: template_body
field.h2: Information Relating to Off-Balance-Sheet Transactions and Commitments

div.p: Sureties, Endorsements, Guarantees, Security Interests and Commitments to Related Entities (Art. 836-1 and 836-2)

div.h3: Sureties, Endorsements, Guarantees, Security Interests and Commitments to Related Entities
div.p: Where applicable, specify the nature and amount of sureties, endorsements, guarantees or security interests given by {{ company name }} during the year.
Where applicable, specify the commitments made to related entities, as well as pension or similar indemnity commitments.

The entity discloses in the notes information relating to any financial commitment, guarantee or contingency not shown on the balance sheet, knowledge of which is necessary to assess the entity's financial position. This information includes in particular:

ul.li: a statement of sureties, endorsements and guarantees given by the entity
a statement of security interests granted by it
firm commitments on equity securities not recognized on the balance sheet, as well as commitments arising from contracts qualified as "warehousing" arrangements
commitments granted on a conditional basis
pension or similar indemnity commitments.

div.p: Commitments made to related entities are disclosed. It is specified that a company is considered related to another when it is likely to be included by full consolidation in the same consolidation scope.
Finance Lease Commitments (Art. 836-3 and 836-4)

p.strong: Lease payments remaining to be paid

div.p: For assets held under a finance lease, the entity discloses the amounts of lease payments remaining to be paid as well as the residual purchase price of these assets stipulated in the contracts, distinguishing between movable and real-property finance lease arrangements.
The disclosures required under Article 836-3 are supplemented by the following information:

ol.li: the value of assets held under a finance lease at the time the contract was signed
the amount of lease payments for the year as well as the cumulative amount of lease payments for prior years

the depreciation charges that would have been recognized for these assets for the year ended had they been acquired by the entity, as well as the cumulative amount of depreciation that would have been recognized for prior years
the measurement of lease payments remaining to be paid as well as the residual purchase price of these assets stipulated in the contracts.

div.p: The information required under the preceding paragraphs, as well as that required under Article 836-3, is broken down according to the balance sheet items to which the relevant assets would have related; the information required under the last paragraph is broken down by maturity: within one year, more than one year and up to five years, and more than five years.
Other Off-Balance-Sheet Transactions (Art. 836-5)

p.strong: Amount of risks and benefits expected from the transaction

div.p: In addition to the information required under Articles 836-1 to 836-4, the entity discloses in the notes information relating to other off-balance-sheet transactions.

An off-balance-sheet transaction is any transaction or agreement between a company and one or more other entities, even if not incorporated as companies, that presents material risks and benefits for a company that are not reflected on the balance sheet and knowledge of which is necessary to assess the company's financial position. The notions of risks and benefits for the company are assessed according to the following criteria:

ul.li: the company bears risks relating to a transaction when it is potentially exposed to an outflow of resources linked to the transaction
the company has the ability to benefit from advantages when it is entitled, directly or indirectly, to the positive resource flows generated by the transaction.

div.p: Whenever the transaction is likely to have a material impact on the entity's financial position, information is provided comprising:

ol.li: a description of the nature and objectives of the transaction
an indication of the amount of risks and benefits expected from the transaction over the entire term of the agreement
an indication of the guarantees given in connection with the transaction
any other information useful for a proper understanding of the transaction.

field.name: template_body
field.p: The average headcount employed by {{ company name }} during the financial year ended {{ end of period }} amounts to {{ average headcount }}, broken down as follows.

p.strong: Average headcount employed during the year

div.p: Mention is made of the headcount employed during the year as defined in Article D. 123-200 of the French Commercial Code.
The information required under Article 837-1 is broken down by category.

field.name: template_body
field.p: The following additional information concerns {{ company name }} for the financial year ended {{ end of period }}, to the extent that the corresponding transactions concern it.

div.p: Warrants and Securities Giving Access to Capital (Art. 838-1)

div.h3: Warrants and Securities Giving Access to Capital
div.p: Specify the issuance terms of warrants or securities giving access to outstanding capital, the movements during the year, and the effect of potential dilution on earnings per share.
The notes disclose the following information:

ol.li:
Share subscription warrants until their expiry date:
issuance terms: amount of the issue, number of warrants, exercise price, exercise deadline
movements in warrants: number of warrants exercised and amount received, number of warrants bought back and cancelled, number of warrants outstanding, potential capital increase in number of shares and in value, trends in the prices of warrants and shares
effect of potential dilution on earnings per share.

Bond subscription warrants until their expiry date:
issuance terms: amount of the issue, number of warrants, exercise price, exercise deadline
movements in warrants: number of warrants exercised and amount received, number of warrants bought back and cancelled, number of warrants outstanding, potential new borrowing in value and in number of bonds, trends in the prices of warrants and bonds.

Bonds with bond subscription warrants until the bonds' maturity and the warrants' expiry date:
issuance terms: amount of the issue, number and nominal value of the bonds, repayment terms, interest rate, number of warrants, exercise price, exercise deadline
movements in bonds: number of bonds outstanding, amount outstanding, number of bonds bought back or redeemed as disclosed in the notes, any impact on income of bond buybacks during the year
movements in warrants: number of warrants exercised and amount received, number of warrants bought back and cancelled, number of warrants outstanding, trends in warrant prices.

Bonds with share subscription warrants until the bonds' maturity and the warrants' expiry date:
issuance terms: amount of the issue, number and nominal value of the bonds, repayment terms, interest rate, number of warrants and exercise price, exercise deadline
movements in bonds: number of bonds outstanding, amount outstanding, number of bonds bought back or redeemed during the year, any impact on income of bond buybacks during the year
movements in warrants: number of warrants exercised, amount received, number of warrants bought back and cancelled, number of warrants outstanding, potential capital increase in number of shares and in value, trends in the prices of warrants and shares
effect of potential dilution on earnings per share.
Shares with share subscription warrants until the expiry date of these warrants: same information as that required under (a) of this article.

div.p: Option Plans and Free Share Award Plans (Art. 838-2)

div.h3: Option Plans and Free Share Award Plans
div.p: Specify the main characteristics of the current option plan or free share award plan, the amount of the expense recognized for the year, and the amount of the liability recorded on the balance sheet.
The notes disclose the following information:

ul.li:
the main characteristics of the plan:
exercise price (for share purchase and subscription option plans)
total number of shares that may be issued or purchased
value of shares used as the basis for the social contribution
conditions for the vesting of shares or the exercise of purchase options (performance, presence)
number of shares or options granted during the year and during the prior year
cumulative number of shares or options granted since the grant date, for each plan
information on contingent liabilities (open choice between the allotment of new shares or existing shares)
the number of cancelled options (for option plans)
the amount of the expense recognized during the year and during the prior year
the amount of the liability recorded on the balance sheet
the detail of account 502 (number of shares, entry cost) and information on the allocation between the two sub-accounts and the corresponding impairment.

div.p: Guaranteed Value Certificates (Art. 838-3)

Specify the market value of the securities, the number of securities not bought back, the characteristics of the securities issued, and the maximum amount of commitments represented by the guarantee, for any guaranteed value certificate or similar instrument issued.
Entities issuing guaranteed value certificates, guaranteed value transfer warrants and similar instruments disclose in the notes, between the issuance of the securities and their maturity:

ul.li: the market value of the securities at the date the accounts are prepared
the number of securities not bought back for cancellation at that date
the characteristics of the securities issued
the maximum amount of commitments represented by the guarantee.

div.p: Long-Term Contracts (Art. 838-4)

Specify, for each ongoing long-term contract, the method used (completed contract or percentage-of-completion), the method used to calculate the percentage of completion, and the amount of provisions for losses on completion.
The entity describes the approach used to apply accounting principles relating to long-term contracts, where applicable by category of contract, specifying in particular:

ul.li: the possible inclusion of financial expenses in allocable costs
the amount of provisions for losses on completion as well as their movement during the year
where the entity is unable to determine the provision corresponding to the most likely loss scenario, a description of the additional risk measured relative to the lowest loss scenario
where the entity is unable to reasonably estimate the amount of any provision for loss on completion, the existence and nature of the uncertainty
the method used to calculate the percentage of completion where the entity applies the percentage-of-completion method
whether, in determining the effect of a change of method, the estimate of the result on completion at the closing of the year of the change was taken into account.

div.p: Advertising Barter Transactions (Art. 838-5)
Specify the amounts retained in income and expenses in respect of barter transactions involving an advertising service.

Entities disclose in the notes the amounts retained in income and expenses relating to barter transactions in which at least one of the items exchanged relates to an advertising service, for each year presented.

For barter transactions mentioned in the preceding paragraph whose market value could not be reliably determined, information is provided on the volume and type of advertising (or other) granted or obtained.
Greenhouse Gas Emission Allowances and Energy Savings Certificates (Art. 838-6 and 838-7)

div.h3: Greenhouse Gas Emission Allowances and Energy Savings Certificates
div.p: Specify the economic model(s) used for greenhouse gas emission allowances or energy savings certificates, the estimated emissions or savings achieved, and the assumptions used to measure the liability.
The notes disclose the following information:

ul.li: a description of the economic model(s) used to manage and account for emission allowances ("Production" model, "Trading" model)
the estimated greenhouse gas emissions achieved
the assumptions taken into account for measuring the "emission allowances to be acquired" liability
any relevant information on CO2 risk management.

div.p: Since allowances are allocated for multi-year allocation periods and then issued to companies in annual tranches, entities must show under "Commitments received" the portion of allowances remaining to be received for the current allocation period.
Information relating to energy savings certificates (ESC):

ul.li: Description of the economic model(s) for managing and accounting for ESCs ("Energy savings" model, "Trading" model)
Description of the assumptions taken into account to measure the liability
Any relevant information on ESC management
Amount of advances paid under financial incentive schemes.

div.p: Rebates, Future Financial Commitments and Transfer of Debt Servicing (Art. 838-8 and 838-9)

div.h3: Rebates, Future Financial Commitments and Transfer of Debt Servicing
div.p: Specify the amount of rebates or reductions obtained or granted, as well as future financial commitments given or received.
Specify the financial consequences and the overall cost of transferring the servicing of a debt, as well as the amount remaining to be repaid.
The notes disclose, for the debtor and for the creditor, the amounts relating to:

ul.li: rebates and/or reductions obtained or granted
future financial commitments given or received.

div.p: The entity that transfers the servicing of the debt discloses, at the time the transaction is carried out, its financial consequences and its overall cost. Until the debt is legally extinguished, it provides information on the transaction, in particular the amount remaining to be repaid included in financial commitments.
Repurchase Agreements and Financial Collateral Arrangements with Right of Reuse (Art. 838-10 and 838-11)

div.h3: Repurchase Agreements and Financial Collateral Arrangements with Right of Reuse
div.p: Specify the nature of the assets given or received as collateral and the amount of the corresponding commitments, for any repurchase agreement on securities or any financial collateral arrangement with a right of reuse.
The notes include the following information:

ul.li: disclosure by the transferor of the commitment received from the transferee, by type of security, and the agreed price

disclosure by the transferee of the commitment given to the transferor, by type of security, and the agreed price. In the event of a discount on the current value of the securities, the reason for not recognizing a provision is specified.

div.p: The notes disclose, for the grantor:

ul.li: the nature of the assets pledged as collateral under financial collateral arrangements with a right of reuse
the amount of commitments given in respect of assets pledged as collateral under a financial collateral arrangement with a right of reuse
the amount of assets pledged as collateral and transferred in full ownership under financial collateral arrangements with a right of reuse.

div.p: The notes disclose, for the beneficiary:

ul.li: the nature of the assets received as collateral under financial collateral arrangements with a right of reuse
the amount of commitments received in respect of assets received as collateral under a financial collateral arrangement with a right of reuse
the amount of assets received in full ownership under financial collateral arrangements with a right of reuse.

div.p: Trust Arrangements (Fiducie) (Art. 838-12)
Specify the purpose and duration of the trust agreement, the identity of the other parties, and the nature of the assets and liabilities transferred.
a) The notes disclose, for the settlor:

ul.li:
the trust agreement(s) entered into, specifying:
the purpose and duration of the agreement(s)
the identity of the other settlor(s) and the trustee
the main terms of the agreement, including in particular the specific arrangements for assuming liabilities (reference to the second paragraph of Article 2025 of the French Civil Code) and the contractual provisions relating to cash transfers from the trust to the settlor

the nature of the assets and liabilities transferred or to be transferred, specifying:
the gross value, depreciation, impairment, and net carrying amount
the measurement approach used at the time of transfer.

div.p: b) The notes disclose, for the trustee:

ul.li: the list and nature of trust agreements entered into and of separate accounts established as trustee

for each agreement, an indication of whether the agreement provides that, in the event of insufficient assets, all or part of the shortfall is to be borne by the trustee (reference to the second paragraph of Article 2025 of the French Civil Code).

div.p: c) The notes disclose, for the beneficiary, when not the settlor:

ul.li:
the trust agreement(s) entered into, specifying:
the purpose and duration of the agreement(s)
the identity of the settlor(s) and the trustee

the nature of the assets and liabilities transferred or to be transferred by the settlor(s) into the trust:
the nature of the consideration granted to the settlor(s)
the nature of the rights or obligations accruing to the beneficiary.

div.p: d) If the settlor is not the beneficiary of all or part of the rights, information is provided on the identity of the beneficiary(ies) and the nature of the rights and obligations transferred or to be transferred:

ul.li: the table of movements in accounts 2661 "Rights representing net assets transferred to a trust" and 162 "Obligations representing net liabilities transferred to a trust", detailed by agreement
the arrangements for allocating the result of each agreement.

div.p: Derivative Financial Instruments and Hedging Transactions (Art. 838-13)

div.h3: Derivative Financial Instruments and Hedging Transactions
div.p: Specify, for each category of derivative financial instruments or hedging transactions, the fair value if determinable, the volume and nature of the instruments, as well as the hedging strategy pursued.
The notes include the following information:
1- Derivative financial instruments
For each category of derivative financial instruments:

ol.li: the fair value of the instruments, if this value can be determined by reference to a market value or by applying generally accepted valuation models and techniques
indications on the volume and nature of the instruments (product type, underlying).

div.p: This information is given in connection with the description of hedging strategies.
For hedging transactions, the amount of realized gains and losses deferred on the balance sheet is specified in connection with hedging strategies.
2- Hedging strategies
Narrative information is given on the hedging strategies pursued, specifying in particular the use of optimization transactions with or without additional risk-taking.
Mergers and Similar Transactions (Art. 838-14)

Specify the context of the merger, demerger or partial asset contribution transaction, the measurement approach used for the contributions, and the treatment of any merger surplus or deficit recognized.

ol.li: For all transactions falling within the scope of Title VII of Book II, the absorbing entity or the entity benefiting from the contributions must disclose the impact of the transaction on the main balance sheet and income statement items, and the following information in the notes to its annual accounts for the year of the transaction:

ul.li: the entity must disclose the context of the transaction, the measurement approach used for the contributions, as well as any adoption of the exemptions provided for under Title VII of Book II (spin-off of a business division and insufficient net book value of assets contributed to allow the capital to be paid up)
where a transaction has resulted in the recognition of a surplus, the entity must disclose the treatment adopted

where a transaction has resulted in the recognition of a deficit, the entity must disclose the material items to which the deficit has been allocated, as well as the depreciation, impairment and final derecognition arrangements for the deficit
where an interim loss and/or badwill is recognized, the entity must disclose the amount recorded in the merger premium sub-account

in the case of the spin-off of a business division intended to be transferred to an entity under separate control, where the contributions are measured at fair value, the entity must disclose the intra-group disposal result recognized, in order to prevent the early distribution of income before the disposal outside the group is completed.

ol.li: At each closing, the entity must disclose in the notes the tracking of the deficit allocated to assets, detailing by asset the gross value and, where applicable, depreciation, depreciation reversals, impairment and impairment reversals.

div.p: Tokens and Digital Assets (Art. 838-15 and 838-16)
Specify the context and purpose of each token issuance, the rights and obligations attached, as well as the number and amount of tokens held.

ol.li: Token issuers disclose in the notes:

ul.li: a description of the context and purpose of each issuance

information on the rights and obligations attached to the tokens issued:
the nature of the tokens issued and a description of the characteristics of the explicit or implicit rights and obligations attached to them (e.g., goods and/or services to be delivered, or debts)
where tokens present different natures of rights and obligations, the arrangements for allocating amounts subscribed to the various natures and their respective accounting treatment
where applicable, a statement of the absence of explicit or implicit rights and obligations, and an explanation of the facts and circumstances of this type of issuance
a description of any clauses and triggering events likely to modify or interrupt the rights and obligations initially attached to the tokens, as well as the accounting consequences should each triggering event occur
the recognition principles for income relating to tokens issued, in particular the approach used to recognize deferred revenue in turnover
where applicable, the amount of borrowings and similar debts that are repayable in tokens or indexed to the value of tokens, as well as the methods or changes in methods for determining the values used for these tokens
the following general information relating to the tokens issued:
the trend in the price of the token issued on the secondary market, its price at year-end, specifying the method used to determine the reference price at the closing date
the schedule and conditions for issuing tokens during future years
the number of tokens issued and remaining to be issued, as well as the reasons for changes during the year, specifying the number of tokens granted free of charge or on preferential terms, as well as any availability restrictions on these tokens granted free of charge or on preferential terms. Where applicable, it is stated whether the number of tokens remaining to be issued is unlimited.

ol.li: Token holders disclose in the notes:

ul.li: the number and amount of tokens held under Article 619-11, whether they are amortizable or non-amortizable, their market value, as well as any impairment recognized
the number and amount of tokens held under Article 619-12, specifying the method used to determine the market values used, and the method for taking available quotations into account
the number and value of tokens held by the company itself, under Article 619-14
the number and value of tokens held that have been pledged as collateral
the use of the first-in, first-out method, or the weighted average acquisition cost method
the number and value of tokens borrowed.

div.p: Digital asset service providers disclose in the notes any relevant information reflecting their activity, and in particular:

ul.li: commitments relating to outstanding placement guarantees on digital assets, mentioned in point (e) of 5° of Article L. 54-10-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code

where providing a custody service for digital assets on behalf of third parties, as mentioned in 1° of Article L. 54-10-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code:
the designation and number of digital assets held in custody on behalf of third parties, not recognized as assets of the digital asset service providers pursuant to point 1 of Article 629-1
the amount of indexed liabilities for the return of digital assets held in custody, where digital asset service providers recognize them on their balance sheet pursuant to point 2 of Article 629-1.

div.p: Professional Training (Art. 838-17)

If the entity wishes to disclose it, specify the amount spent on professional training during the year, the prior year and the last three years combined, as well as its breakdown by type of training and in the relevant income statement or balance sheet items.
The entity may disclose the following information relating to professional training:

ol.li:
Amount spent on professional training:
during the year
during the prior year
during the last three years, indicating the cumulative amount amortized over three years.
This amount is broken down by type of training.
Breakdown of this amount in the main income statement or balance sheet items (if training costs are capitalized under the provisions of Articles 213-8 and 213-22)
Amount spent on professional training relative to the payroll
Number of training hours
Proportion of staff who received training during the year.

div.p: Non-repayable Funds and Conditional Advances (Art. 838-18)
Specify the characteristics of non-repayable funds or conditional advances shown on the liabilities side: instruments issued or financing received, remuneration terms, repayment terms and maturity.
Information relating to non-repayable funds and conditional advances includes:
1- a breakdown of the amounts shown at the closing of the year:

ul.li: for the non-repayable funds line: the detail is given by instrument presenting the same repayment and remuneration characteristics
for the conditional advances line: a distinction is made between the portion relating to the principal amount and that relating to accrued interest

div.p: 2- details on the characteristics of the instruments issued and recorded as non-repayable funds and of the financing received and recorded as conditional advances. The entity discloses, in particular, the remuneration terms, the repayment terms and the maturity
3- for any amount of accrued interest attached to conditional advances, the payment terms and the payment due date.
Remuneration of a Service by an Equity Instrument to Be Issued (Art. 838-19)

div.h3: Remuneration of a Service by an Equity Instrument to Be Issued
div.p: Specify the total number of equity securities to be issued and the amount of reserves used, for any remuneration of a service by means of an equity instrument to be issued.

In respect of the remuneration of a service by means of an equity instrument to be issued, the debtor entity discloses, in the notes, the total number of equity securities to be issued as well as the amount of reserves used when the instrument is issued.

field.p: The financing table of {{ company name }} for the financial year ended {{ end of period }} is shown below.

div.p: Preparation Principles

The financing table is prepared based on the cash flows relating to operating, investing and financing activities for the year (where applicable, specify the adjustments made and the definition of net cash used).
Adjustments made and definition of net cash used, if different from the standard method.

Entities falling within the scope of Articles L. 232-2 and L. 612-2 of the French Commercial Code are required to prepare a financing table. The financing table is accompanied by information on the principles that governed its preparation.
